items.title: Joey Morant interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2013
items.q: Mostly gospel, R&B, 78 records. Ruth Brown, Rasheed Young, Mahalia Jackson...

ctx.x: What kind of music was being played in your home?
Mostly gospel, R&B, 78 records. Ruth Brown, Rasheed Young, Mahalia Jackson, the lady that recorded “Fine Brown Frame” who was that, a delegate to Union 47, Nellie © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

Lutcher, [sings] Fine Brown Frame/I wonder what could be his name. She also recorded a song called “My Mother’s Eye” was the name of the song. A standard. And I recorded that on my latest CD. “My Mother’s Eye.” A tribute to mothers. Nellie Lutcher, who had a hit record in ’48, who ended up being a delegate in the union, Local 47, Los Angeles. So I picked my samples from things in the air, and when I was sick in the hospital — I was in the hospital a lot — and they had the metal posts on the bed where you could…
